data.title: Estée Lauder CEO praises travel retail, online sales as Q1 net sales grow 6%
data.description:
The Estée Lauder Companies Inc. reported increases in online sales in Asia and in its travel retail business during the company’s fiscal first quarter ended Sept. 30.

The Health & Beauty brand raised its outlook for fiscal 2027, citing improved profitability in Q1 as net sales grew 6.7% year over year to $3.7 billion.

Estée Lauder is No. 42 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Estée Lauder is also No. 310 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Why Estée Lauder raised its outlook for 2027

“The energy and determination of our teams, combined with the strength of our brands and the progress of our transformation, give me greater confidence than ever in the opportunities that lie ahead,” said Stéphane de La Faverie, president and CEO at Estée Lauder. “We are raising our fiscal 2027 outlook, reflecting both our strong start and our conviction in the future we are creating.”

The company now expects to see organic net sales growth of 4.0% to 5.5% instead of its previously forecast 3% to 5% in its full 2027 fiscal year.

In its earnings release, Estée Lauder credited what it characterized as “strong performance in the fiscal 2027 first quarter,” even as it stayed “cautious amid ongoing geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty.”

Highlights for the quarter included expanded availability through online channels, as well as successes in Asia and travel retail.

Where Estée Lauder online sales grew in Q1

Estée Lauder reported that it widened online consumer availability of its products on Amazon, where the company claimed to now have 13 brands across 17 markets. In the meantime, it also expanded to 15 brands present across 11 markets on TikTok Shop.

Its online sales encompass direct sales from its individual brands and retailers’ ecommerce sites, as well as through third-party platforms.

Specifically, the company noted online sales growth in Asia, where its new fulfillment center in China’s Hainan province opened in July, as well as in its travel retail business division.

“We delivered high-single-digit organic sales growth online [in Q1], driven by both established platform and expansion,” said de La Faverie on an earnings call with investors. “Encouragingly, online growth was also well balanced.”

He characterized growth broadly across regions.

“Asia Pacific rose double digit, while each of the other three regions grew high-single digits,” he stated. “In the U.S. and China, we gained share online with retail sales growth more than 2x faster than the industry in our two biggest markets.”

Estée Lauder’s investments in digital infrastructure

Estée Lauder, which uses Shopify as an ecommerce platform, extended use for M·A·C and Clinique brands’ sites in the U.S. and U.K. over the past quarter, as M·A·C physical stores also opened up in those markets.

Continued modernizing its digital technology infrastructure to deliver best-in-class consumer experiences with the full deployment of Shopify for M·A·C and Clinique on their US and UK brand.com, as well as the initial rollout for M·A·C freestanding stores in the US and UK.

In addition, Akhil Shrivastava, the chief financial officer at Estée Lauder, credited Shopify as a part of the company’s digital efforts, enabling what he called “superior consumer experiences, greater speed, simpler processes and improved productivity.”

“This can be seen in our Shopify deployment and the partnering with Profound, an AI marketing platform, bringing global insights into how our brands appear across AI platforms,” he stated.

data.title: Watsco updates on acquisitions as ecommerce sales rise 10% in Q3
data.description:
Watsco has bulked up with the acquisition of two regional rivals. The heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) distributor also reported record third-quarter sales of $2.22 billion, up 7%, as acquisitions and a growing ecommerce business offset slimmer margins. Ecommerce made up 37% of the distributor’s revenue over the past year, and its newest acquisitions, Jackson Supply and The Granite Group, added roughly $730 million in revenue.

The company highlighted HVAC equipment as its largest business segment, at 67% of sales, which will be bolstered by the acquisitions of the two companies, starting with Jackson Supply in a deal that closed in June. Jackson has $230 million in annual sales and operates from 25 Sunbelt locations. Jackson, Watsco said, is performing well and grew 16% during the quarter.

The Granite Group, which Watsco acquired in October, is another acquisition in the HVAC space. Granite has annual sales of approximately $500 million and serves approximately 11,000 customers from 82 locations in the Northeast.

Watsco has been an active buyer. Granite is the fourth business it has acquired that serves dual-trade HVAC and plumbing contractors.

Albert Nahmad, Watsco’s chairman and CEO, credited digital with being a big part of the company’s growth.

Watsco ecommerce sales in Q3

“Our digital ecosystem is producing measurable results and driving growth,” Nahmad said.

Ultimately, Watsco ecommerce sales grew 10% year over year in Q3. The company reported that they were also up 12% for the nine-month period ended Sept. 30, outpacing the distributor’s overall revenue growth.

Mobile app use is a big part of that ecosystem.

Nahmad said that digital engagement with the company’s mobile apps is strong, with more than 73,000 active monthly users. He also said that the OnCallAir digital sales platform continues to grow, with approximately 351,000 proposals presented to homeowners, generating $2 billion in gross merchandise value, a 14% increase over the comparable period.

“Simply put, the contractors we serve digitally are growing faster, have greater loyalty, and we believe we can lower our cost to serve at scale over time,” Nahmad said. “Just as exciting, the new initiatives announced late last year are making progress.”

Nahmad pointed to how fragmented the residential HVAC market is, but that they remain a market leader in consolidating that business.

“Year-to-date, operating cash flow has improved 79% to $304 million, reflecting our continued vigilance towards managing our assets,” Nahmad assessed.

Contractors said the shift online comes down to price and speed.

Online trends for HVAC sales

Dan Blizman, owner of Blizzard Mechanical, a commercial-focused HVAC service and installation company based in Connecticut, said price and availability are driving contractors online.

“I would say both price and availability are two of the largest driving factors behind contractors ordering from online versus local distributors,” Blizman said. “I know in our own experience it is often both cheaper and faster to get something from an online vendor than a local supply house.”

Blizman said as long as the level of support stays the same, he does not expect that purchasing smaller, regional distributors will disrupt business.

“Keep the level of support and attention the same as it was or improve it, on top of the price and availability,” he said. “Give us all three and you get serious loyalty.”

Watsco’s recent acquisitions

Michael Ligon, strategic capital investor at The Ligon Group, a Florida firm that buys real estate and privately owned businesses, said that for an owner of an HVAC distribution business thinking about selling, the real question is not whether to sell; it is which option fits the situation.

“When a business is clean, growing, and easy for a buyer to underwrite, a straight sale to a consolidator like Watsco can be a genuinely good option: strong price, clean exit, and in Watsco’s case the Jackson Supply and Granite Group deals show the name, management, and culture can stay intact,” Ligon said

He noted that being acquired can be a best-case path, and he believes owners who can take such deals should do so.

“Watsco’s run, roughly $730 million in acquired sales this year alone in a fragmented $74 billion market, proves the demand is there,” Ligon stated.

Percentage changes may not align exactly with dollar figures due to rounding. Check back for more earnings reports. Here’s our last update on Watsco ecommerce sales.

data.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
data.description:
DoorDash Inc. announced a deal to acquire its last-mile delivery rival Instacart in a deal valued at $17 billion.

The combined company would unite operations from two of the most active platforms in retail and grocery delivery services through a transaction subject to approval by regulators and Instacart shareholders. DoorDash expects to use a combination of cash, stock and debt to finance the deal. As a result, the acquisition would enable DoorDash to leverage Instacart’s technology and expertise.

Why DoorDash is acquiring Instacart

“Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online,” said Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of DoorDash, in the acquisition announcement. “Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts.”

Xu praised the work that Instacart has done to date.

“Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day,” he stated. “Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery. It’s still early innings, but we know that when more people shop local, more dollars stay local.”

Online grocery sales in the U.S. grew by more than 20% year over year, increasing their share of total grocery spending, according to data tracked by the firm Brick Meets Click.

What comes next for Instacart

DoorDash and Instacart expect the deal to close near the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028, the companies disclosed. After that, DoorDash expects to preserve the Instacart brand, along with its enterprise technology products and app. In the meantime, Instacart intends to continue to operate independently.

“Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more,” said Chris Rogers, CEO of Instacart. “When our purpose-built grocery technology and trusted retailer and brand relationships are combined with DoorDash’s global consumer reach and logistics capabilities, we can create new opportunities for our retail and brand partners, offer an even better experience for customers and shoppers, and deliver compelling value for our shareholders.”

In the announcement, DoorDash noted that it could make 50,000 additional stores available to Instacart users through the deal, adding to almost 100,000 stores that already participate on Instacart’s platform.

data.title: GME acquires regional rival Commercial Supply Co.
data.description:
Two Midwestern workplace safety distributors have joined forces, with GME Supply acquiring Commercial Supply Co.

GME Supply, a Columbia, Missouri-based distributor of workplace safety gear and equipment, announced the deal, which will welcome its Des Moines, Iowa-based competitor into its portfolio. CSC is a distributor that primarily serves construction and industrial contractors. The deal extends GME’s reach across the Midwest and adds inventory and specialty products such as cable-wrapping equipment and industrial textiles. Commercial Supply’s two co-owners, Brad Lilienthal and Jason Curry, will join GME. Terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Why GME Supply is acquiring Commercial Supply Co.

GME’s top executive laid out its reasoning behind the CSC acquisition.

“Commercial Supply has earned a strong reputation by understanding what contractors need and delivering solutions that keep projects moving,” said Ryan Keogh, CEO of GME Supply.

Keogh touched upon the benefits expected from the acquisition.

“Their expertise, customer relationships, and entrepreneurial approach are a natural fit with GME Supply,” he stated. “Together, we can offer customers broader capabilities, greater access to inventory, and the resources to support projects across more markets.”

Lilienthal also praised the move.

“Joining GME Supply creates exciting opportunities for our customers and employees,” Lilienthal said. “With access to a broader range of products, additional resources and a national distribution network, we can build on what we’ve established and serve more customers across more markets.”

The marriage adds to a digital operation GME has worked to build. Its ecommerce sites, GME.com and FWLSP.com, run an ordering platform designed for large-scale customers, and Keogh described the company as “digital first” in a 2024 interview with Industrial Supply Magazine. GME also owns Gearcor, whose software lets companies run uniform, PPE, and fall protection ordering through a private online marketplace with a manager dashboard.

Business implications for the acquisition

Industry analysts said the move made sense.

Alex Stepansky, founder of Corridome, a database of U.S. private equity firms, M&A advisers and deals built from public records, noted that GME Supply is owned by Incline Equity Partners, a Pittsburgh-based private equity firm, “so Commercial Supply Co. is an add-on: a PE-owned distributor buying a smaller regional one,” Stepansky said.

He said buying a smaller rival distributor can make sense in this scenario.

“A regional distributor comes with branches, contractor accounts and supplier lines that would take years to build,” he stated. “Small distributors also tend to sell for a lower multiple of earnings than a larger platform does, so each add-on raises what the owner can sell the whole company for later.”

When Incline Equity Partners bought GME in 2023, the company said it planned to improve its online ordering platform.

For customers, the change usually shows up online first, Stepansky assessed.

“The smaller company’s buyers get moved onto the parent’s ordering site and catalog,” he added.

Why digital strengths are important

Mike Danford, owner and chief revenue officer at Adverio, an omni-marketplace operator that runs marketplace operations for ecommerce brands, said the digital piece is what GME brings to the table.

“GME runs its own purchasing platform, GME PRO, and a managed-gear program under the Gearcor name, where a contractor sets allowances and approved catalogs and the crew orders its own PPE from a phone,” Danford pointed out.

He added that Commercial Supply brings solar and wind contractors whose crews need exactly that. Thus, the value is moving those accounts onto GME’s system with the Des Moines team as the face.

“The risk is the migration,” he said. “Across the brands we manage, business buyers are already 8% to 9% of sales catalog-wide and about 20% in some categories.”

Danford said, noting that this can be the demand a distributor leaks when its checkout is slower than a marketplace, and the months after an acquisition are when a manager tries Amazon Business for the first time.

“Make the contractor relearn how to order and the marketplace siphons the new business,” Danford said.

He anticipates that the deal will work best if it is a seamless merger where the customer detects nothing new.

“Same rep, same credit terms, same truck,” he stated. “It fails when the first thing the customer notices is a new login, higher prices, and a product that didn’t survive the catalog cut. Contractors rarely switch distributors over a merger. They switch over the week an order didn’t show up.”

data.title: Bark revenue falls despite commerce growth resuming in Q2
data.description:
Bark net revenue and direct-to-consumer (DTC) revenue both declined in the company’s fiscal second quarter ended Sept. 30. However, the seller of pet products managed to reignite growth for its commerce revenue — which comes from sales with retail partners — and prepare the sale of its dog-focused airline as it sought to correct course for its business.

Overall, net revenue fell 18.1% year over year to $87.6 million in Q2, weighed down by reduced subscriber activity in its DTC sales.

Bark is No. 261 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Bark is also No. 806 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Bark web sales by year

Bark revenue in Q2

“Commerce returned to growth, Subscriber Retention improved to 94%, and we put our marketing dollars to work where they were most efficient,” said Matt Meeker, co-founder and CEO at Bark. “We also made meaningful progress expanding our product offerings and retail presence, including the launch of Licksters, our new line of enrichment toys, and the shipment of two of the largest retail orders in Bark’s history during our fiscal third quarter.”

Commerce net revenue in Q2 increased 3.6% from a year ago to reach $25.7 million. Meanwhile, DTC revenue declined 24.7% to $61.8 million over the same period.

Meeker addressed key challenges that have hindered growth at Bark in recent years. As he did so, he laid out Bark’s timeline for getting rid of its Bark Air, the dog airline service that launched in May 2024.

Selling Bark Air

“Subsequent to quarter end, we reached a preliminary understanding to sell Bark Air’s assets and license the brand beginning January 1, 2027,” Meeker stated. “The arrangement remains subject to definitive documentation and there is no assurance it will be completed.’

Assuming the deal goes through, Meeker expects Bark to be able to redirect funds toward its commerce operations, partnerships, supply chain and innovation efforts.

Bark Air originally debuted with service to New York, Los Angeles and London, later expanding to Paris, Lisbon, Madrid, Seattle, South Florida and San Francisco. The service eyed dogs and their human companions, offering specialized accommodations for them to travel together in the air. In addition, Bark Air offers a Companion Concierge service for travel planning, handling commercial and private flights, as well as ground transportation.
